When Eva studies English for ministry, her goal is not simply to collect impressive words. A ministry language is formed when vocabulary, grammar, Scripture, and love begin to serve one another. Psalm 119:105 describes God's word as a lamp and a light. That image is important for a learner because a lamp usually gives enough light for the next step, not for the whole road at once. In the same way, Eva may not see every future ministry assignment clearly, but she can still practice the next faithful sentence today.
Teacher Ali: Read for main idea, religious terms, connectors, and ministry verbs.

pages.title: Conditionals
pages.subtitle: Meaning
pages.summary: Target: Zero, First, Second, Third, and Mixed conditionals for calling, plans, and hypothetical ministry situations.
blocks: Target: Zero, First, Second, Third, and Mixed conditionals for calling, plans, and hypothetical ministry situations.
Conditionals connect a situation with a result. In ministry English, Eva uses them to talk about calling, preparation, wise choices, and hypothetical service.
Zero: if + present, present. First: if + present, will/can/should. Second: if + past, would/could. Third: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Mixed: past condition + present result.
Use First Conditional for real plans, Second Conditional for imagined ministry situations, Third Conditional for reflection, and Mixed Conditional for testimony.
Do not use will inside the if-clause for normal First Conditional: say If God opens the door, I will prepare, not If God will open.
